title: Closed-Form and Multi-Term Series Solutions for the Three-Dimensional Bending Analysis of Shear-Deformable Orthotropic Rectangular Plates  with a Free Edge
content: Closed-form solutions simplify the design of thick orthotropic plates, but their accuracy for plates with a free edge is unknown. This study developed one-term closed-form and multi-term series solutions of Alternative 1 Theory, with three-dimensional (3D) constitutive relations, for uniformly loaded rectangular orthotropic plates with a free edge. Ten support combinations, with the free edge parallel or perpendicular to the stiff direction, were analysed in 1,200 cases (E1/E2 = 5–40, a/t = 4–20, b/a = 0.5–3.0). A 3D Ritz solution, with deflections within 0.08% of exact, Lévy-type, and finite element solutions, served as the reference, and the series separated shape error from theory error. The converged series underestimated the 3D deflection by 4–19% at a/t = 4 and by up to 10% at a/t = 20. Its error was largest where the stiff direction spans between a clamped and a simply supported edge; there, it also overestimated the clamped-edge moment by up to 129%. Free-edge orientation governed the response. Plates with the free edge across the stiff direction deflected up to 1,050 times as much as their quarter-turned counterparts, and the one-term solution underestimated their deflection by 11–95% for b/a ≥ 1.0. The one-term formulas were within 10% of 3D elasticity in 319 cases, half of them for four plates with a/t ≤ 5 and b/a ≥ 1.0, partly through a cancellation of shape and theory errors. In thick plates, 3D face stresses at the free edge exceeded the linear values by up to 110%.
